content: If someone is experiencing severe symptoms such as losing consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. While using this medication, your healthcare provider may perform laboratory and/or medical tests, such as monitoring your blood pressure, heart rate, electrocardiogram (EKG), and blood potassium levels. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. Store this medication at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. Do not puncture the canister or expose it to high heat or open flames. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. Your medical condition may lead to complications during a medical emergency. Ensure that your healthcare providers are aware of your condition. This information was last revised in May 2024. This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Before using epinephrine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to similar bronchodilators (e.g., albuterol, levalbuterol, salmeterol), to sympathomimetic drugs (e.g., pseudoephedrine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Avoid using MAO inhibitors (e.g., isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue, moclobemide, phenelzine, procarbazine, rasagiline, safinamide, selegiline, tranylcypromine) or tricyclic antidepressants (e.g., amitriptyline, nortriptyline) within two weeks before, during, and after treatment with this medication. Caffeine can increase the side effects of this medication. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. Store this medication at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. Do not puncture the canister or expose it to high heat or open flames. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Your medical condition may lead to complications during a medical emergency. Ensure that your healthcare providers are aware of your condition. This information was last revised in May 2024.
